subject: EchoForge integration: compatibility playbook & L2 test matrix
messages:
From: Alexandra Wu <alex@echoforge.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parker Lim <parker.lim@echoforge.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: EchoForge - Redwood integration: request for compatibility playbook

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for taking this early look. EchoForge is preparing a prospective joint connector to route in-product prompts to Redwood for on-demand inference. Before our architecture sync next week, can you share a short "compatibility playbook" that outlines:

- reference integration patterns (direct API v. brokered via our middleware)
- required auth/keys and recommended rotation cadence
- network constraints and recommended sandbox topology (VPC peering vs. tunnel)
- minimal test matrix for L2 validation (latency, tokenization, streaming)

I've attached our current API spec (echoforge-api-spec-v2.pdf) and a small sample dataset we use in-house. We're aiming to scope a 2-week sandbox validation.

Appreciate any templates/short checklist you can send over.

Alexandra Wu
Head of Integrations, EchoForge
alex@echoforge.ai

Attachment: echoforge-api-spec-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB)

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Wu <alex@echoforge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EchoForge - Redwood integration: request for compatibility playbook

Alexandra — thanks for the context and the spec. High level, Redwood supports two common patterns for partners like EchoForge:

1) Direct API passthrough (recommended for lowest latency): EchoForge calls Redwood's hosted inference API with per-request API key and optional customer-scoped project header. Requires HTTPS outbound from your middleware to Redwood and a short-lived key rotation policy.

2) Brokered connector (recommended if you need in-product telemetry or message transformation): EchoForge hosts a connector service which talks to Redwood Dedicated or Private through a service account; this allows batching/aggregation and extra observability but adds a small 30–80ms tail for broker processing.

Attached is a short scope doc that outlines the interface expectations and a starter checklist (redwood-connector-scope.docx). For the sandbox topology I recommend:
- VPC peering for EchoForge sandbox <> Redwood VPC if you want traffic to stay internal
- fallback: mTLS tunnel using our partner tunnel endpoint for quick POC work

I'll loop Marissa for the L2 test matrix and Hiro for network/security specifics. Proposed next steps:
- Mar 1–14: sandbox validation (we run the test matrix against your sample payloads)
- March 15: joint tech review to sign off on production runbook

Sergio Alvarez
Partner Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-connector-scope.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 48KB)

From: Alexandra Wu <alex@echoforge.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parker Lim <parker.lim@echoforge.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EchoForge - Redwood integration: request for compatibility playbook

Thanks, Sergio. A few clarifications from our side:

- We will need tokenization compatibility notes (how does Redwood handle special tokens, EOS behavior, byte-pair handling) because our UI pre-processes chat history.
- For the sample payloads, attaching a trimmed set (sample_payloads.json) that includes streaming scenarios and multi-turn contexts.
- Sandbox: we can spin up a temporary EchoForge sandbox in us-west1 and grant IP ranges for the peering or tunnel.

Also sharing a short doc with our security contact's requirements. If you can add the minimal evidence list we need to provide to procurement (IP allowlist docs, SOC2 attestation pointer, audit log export format) that will speed the procurement loop.

Best,
Alexandra

Attachment: sample_payloads.json (application/json, 34KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Wu <alex@echoforge.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-16T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: RF: EchoForge integration playbook (draft)

Hi team — attaching a first-draft integration playbook and a concise L2 test matrix. Key items in the workbook (rf-integration-playbook.xlsx):

- Sheet A: Reference designs — Direct API and Brokered connector with sequence diagrams and expected RTT at 256-token and 1024-token windows.
- Sheet B: Auth & key lifecycle — recommended rotation intervals, scopes, and example JWT claims for a service account flow.
- Sheet C: Network options — VPC peering checklist, route table examples, NAT rules for outbound-only peered traffic.
- Sheet D: L2 test matrix (lf-test-matrix.csv) — cases for cold-start, streaming chunk continuity, tokenization drift checks, and failure injection (rate-limit, partial response).

An abbreviated runbook is on the first tab with explicit pass/fail criteria. For Alexandra's procurement ask, I added a short appendix outlining the artifacts we can provide: SOC 2 report pointer, sample audit-log export (JSON lines), and a network-proof template for peering.

Next actions: Sergio/Hiro to confirm the sandbox IP ranges and expected throughput. Alexandra/Parker to give us the sample traffic profile (TPS, avg tokens/request) and any retention constraints for logs.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: rf-integration-playbook.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 160KB); lf-test-matrix.csv (text/csv, 6KB)

From: hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Wu <alex@echoforge.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-18T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: RE: EchoForge integration: compatibility playbook & L2 test matrix

On Thu, Feb 16, 2027 at 14:22, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi team — attaching a first-draft integration playbook and a concise L2 test matrix.

Quick confirmation from infra/security: we can support both peering and tunnel for the sandbox. For peering we'll need:
- EchoForge sandbox project ID and a CIDR range (minimum /28)
- Point of contact for peering setup and a requested maintenance window (we prefer overnight PST)

Throughput notes: for validation we'll allow up to 250 rps burst with baseline throttles at 100 rps for the sandbox project. If your traffic profile exceeds that, request a temporary quota increase via JIRA-EF-1423 (included above).

Procurement evidence: SOC 2 pointer is public (https://redwood.com/security/soc2). Audit logs will be provided as daily JSONL exports for the sandbox project and retained for 30 days by default; retention can be extended under a dedicated contract.

Hiro Tanaka
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai

--
Next steps (concise):
- EchoForge: share sandbox project ID, expected TPS and avg tokens/request by Feb 22
- Redwood: create sandbox project, open peering request and provide credentials for the test harness by Feb 25
- Joint: run L2 matrix Mar 1–14, meet Mar 15 for sign-off
